steps.title: Keep platform .env files closed to group and others with a systemd timer (workaround)

edits.new:
# Written by stackward: plan step paas-env-perms. A workaround, not a fix:
# Coolify and Dokploy write their .env files again on every deploy, often
# readable by group and others. stackward undo --run RUN_ID removes all three
# units (stackward-paas-env-perms.service, .timer and the timers.target.d
# drop-in); by hand: systemctl stop stackward-paas-env-perms.timer, remove the
# three files, systemctl daemon-reload.
# This service only removes group and other permission bits (chmod) of
# those files. It never opens them, so it never reads, copies or logs a
# value, and it never changes an owner.
[Unit]
Description=stackward: close platform .env files to group and others (chmod only)
Documentation=https://github.com/Shironex/stackward/blob/main/docs/plan.md

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/find /data/coolify/applications -xdev -ignore_readdir_race -maxdepth 4 -type f ( -name .env -o -name .env.* ) ! -name .env.example ! -name .env.sample ! -name .env.template ! -name .env.dist ! -name .env.defaults ( -uid 0 -o -uid 9999 ) -perm /077 -exec chmod go-rwx {} +
ExecStart=/usr/bin/find /data/coolify/services -xdev -ignore_readdir_race -maxdepth 4 -type f ( -name .env -o -name .env.* ) ! -name .env.example ! -name .env.sample ! -name .env.template ! -name .env.dist ! -name .env.defaults ( -uid 0 -o -uid 9999 ) -perm /077 -exec chmod go-rwx {} +
ExecStart=/usr/bin/find /data/coolify/source/.env -maxdepth 0 -type f -uid 9999 -perm /027 -exec chmod g-w,o-rwx {} +
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateNetwork=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ProtectHome=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ReadWritePaths=-/data/coolify/applications -/data/coolify/services -/data/coolify/source/.env
CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH CAP_FOWNER

commands.why: close the open .env files once now (chmod only; a failure stops the run here)
start the timer that repeats it every minute; the timers.target drop-in starts it at boot

undo.description: Stop the timer, remove the service, the timer and the timers.target drop-in, and reload systemd. Files the timer already closed keep their modes; undo never opens them again.

notes: A workaround, not a fix: the platform writes its .env files again on every deploy. This installs stackward-paas-env-perms.service and .timer, which every minute and at boot remove the group and other permission bits of those files with chmod. It never reads, copies or logs their contents and never changes their owner. After a deploy a file can stay open for up to a minute.
Off by default: apply runs it only when you name it (--step paas-env-perms). Remove it with one command, stackward undo --run RUN_ID, which stops the timer and removes the three unit files.

Coolify: app and service .env files owned by root or by uid 9999 (the user Coolify's container runs as and its installer gives /data/coolify to) become owner only (chmod go-rwx); the owner keeps reading and writing them, and root reads any mode.

Coolify mounts /data/coolify/source/.env into its container, which reads it as uid 9999: the timer changes it only while uid 9999 owns it, and keeps the owner's and group's read bits (chmod g-w,o-rwx).

An app container that bind mounts its .env and reads it as another user than the file's owner loses access at its next start; apps that get their variables through compose (env_file, what both platforms generate) are not affected. Check your apps after the next deploy.

Left alone, because the platform does not write files as their owner: /data/coolify/applications/d4e5f6/.env.production (uid 1000). They stay reported; close them by hand once you know who reads them.
